I thought I’d post a bit about the current perk drama, specifically the changes to PerkTV Live.

It started a couple weeks ago when Live audio detection when to crap for a lot of users, many couldn’t get it to activate at all and most found it wouldn’t recognize commercials on its own, requiring constant tapping and a lot of crashes.

As many of you may know, beginning on July 8th Live will only pay 3 pts per video for the first 300 pts then drop to 1-2 pts. This is very similar to what happened to PerkTV in late january/early February. After that many users, especially big farmers moved to PerkTV Live to keep their earnings up. This change makes the app much less attractive to farmers or constant tappers., it neuters it just like they did to PerkTV.

This seems to be Perks standard operating procedure, release an app that’s easy to exploit and has very high earning potential, then when it gets popular to drastically cut down on how many points can be made. Both times it’s been preceded by connection problems and app crashes. They use the earlier adopters bonanza to attract as many users as they can then once they are hooked, pull the rug out from under them. Perks strategy is to use the farmers to spread the word, they know they will brag to all their friends about how great Perk is. By the time the bottom drops out, the farmers aren’t useful to Perk anymore, they cost more than they earn for Perk, so Perk doesn’t care if they stay. Perk hopes that those who remain will be the mid to light users that appear to be more involved to Perks advertisers. Wether that’s true I have no idea.

Clearly this was part of the plan from the start, the amounts Perk was giving out last year were far higher than any other mobile advertising app and they required far less interactivity. The heydays were advertising and base building for Perk, we’re now transitioning into the next phase, lower payouts, higher earnings for Perk. Keeping the users happy at the same time is a balancing act that requires a delicate touch, which Perk has never demonstrated.

The important thing about this new order is that you can still make money from Perk, but you have to be agile, you have to adapt. Perk keeps putting out new apps and when one gets nerfed, you have to pay attention and often move on from the old apps. Farmers can’t be lazy and complacent anymore. Many of the new apps require much more interactivity, it’s likely that Perk can charge more for ads because of that. The days of leaving your farm running for hours on end unattended are likely ending.

Don’t make the mistake of thinking I’m making excuses for them, I think this is an untenable business plan that effectively confuses the users and makes Perk seem very hostile to its user base. I think they could have handled this much better, but this is what we have to work with. There is no going back, the early apps and big payouts were advertising, that kind of money is not sustainable. Be glad you made your money when you did.
